why: A complete passage with no holes and a translation (100 elements, 100% identified, key from Meister); Italian. Excerpt only but it is the whole enciphered passage.

label: George Lasry's excerpt and translation (BnF cipher research, 10 Oct 2026)

sample_en: the enterprise is now almost impracticable on the coast of Kent because of the forces the Prince of Orange has stationed there.
why: Long clean French excerpt (f249v, a paragraph) with fluent English translation and no holes; 99.8% of elements identified. Excerpt only of a 17-page set.

label: R8347, Mary to Archbishop Hamilton, Bolton 18 Jan 1569
sample_original: I pray zow not to communicat to ony man except to thais of quhome ze ar assurit, and in the meane ze haif al reddi begun that ze mak sik demonstration as it may be knawin that ze nor the rest of my faithful subiectis wyl never condescend
sample_en: I pray you not to communicate it to anyone except those of whom you are assured; and meanwhile that you make such a demonstration that it may be known that neither you nor the rest of my faithful subjects will ever consent.
why: Transcription of the contemporary Scots decipherment (ff. 74r-v) on the leaf, line by line; sentences build despite Older Scots spelling; the few unresolved code signs are left as ⟨E⟩, ⟨X⟩, ⟨ʗ⟩ (the decipherer himself copied them through). Needs only modern-English rendering.

label: R1182, Rodrigo Niño (Naples) to Charles V, 19 March 1522: the eight-line cipher block (George Lasry, CTTS)
sample_original: Por amor de Dios suplico a V.M. mande que de España se remedie a la paga desta retaguarda, porque ni ellos tienen pan de que bivir
sample_en: For the love of God I beg Your Majesty to order that the pay of this rearguard be remedied from Spain, because they have no bread to live on.
why: Eight lines of fluent punctuated Spanish (edited form) with no holes; the literal form has two '?' where the key lacks a sign. A single short cipher block, fully read; translation_en.txt also exists.

label: TNA SP 78/129 f. 180, Perwich to Arlington, Paris, 9 April 1670
sample_original: The souldiers grumble much that the king is of late growne cool towards them and gives them not the encouragement in their addresses as hee used.
sample_en: (already English) The soldiers grumble much that the king has lately grown cool towards them and does not give them the encouragement in their addresses that he used to.
why: Full 17th-century English paragraph (The National Archives' published reading); five nomenclator numbers (97, 60, 96, 61, 40) stay as digits and unpunctuated; otherwise fluent. The project's own letter-by-letter output is run-together but the TNA reading is the usable text.

label: Wolff to Wilhelmina, Princess of Orange, The Hague, 25 July 1801 (DECODE R2232)
sample_original: Outre cela j'ai offert à feu le prince Frédéric de lui amener quelques milles hommes de la brigade suisse avec l'élite des officiers, par une lettre que j'ai expédiée le matin du 14 septembre 1795, jour que je fus arrêté
sample_en: Besides that, I offered the late Prince Frederick to bring him some thousands of men of the Swiss brigade with the pick of the officers, by a letter I sent on the morning of 14 September 1795, the day I was arrested.
why: reading.txt is punctuated, modernised French with deciphered parts bracketed; flowing sentences, with a handful of [...] / [?] holes in the last page (P1). The raw decrypt is lower-case run-on with caps for cipher, but the reading file supplies the usable text.

label: R902, Słupca, 15 Oct 1707
sample_original: J'avoue de bonne foy qu'elles me manquent, [9] outre que le malheur que j'ay eu d'estre soupçonné de Vostre Altesse me fait comprendre que la continuation de mes services ne luy seroit pas agreable.
sample_en: I frankly admit that I lack them, besides which the misfortune of having been suspected by Your Highness makes me understand that the continuation of my services would not be agreeable to him.
why: Punctuated French with normalised spelling; the first page (p. 277) and p. 278 lines 1-9 build into long sentences with scattered bracketed group numbers (about ten holes across ~25 lines, e.g. [85], [120], a closing [224 264 174 226 37 / 324 125 104 589 4]); lines 10-18 are a group-by-group table plus a short continuous reading. Translatable.

label: Siena, Concistoro 2308 fasc. 2 no. 25 (DECODE R4813), undated
sample_original: E però richordiamo a la signioria vostra che ne' detti luoghi faciate provedere di pane, biada, vituagia, chome vi pare chovenirsi
sample_en: And so we remind Your Lordship that in the said places you should have bread, fodder and victuals provided, as seems fitting to you.
why: File ends with a punctuated running Italian text (Sienese spelling) and an English summary; 96.2% of tokens read, only 'TH' (one sign) unread and two doubtful words (s'hadra, o chon grediamo). Short letter, fully coherent.

label: Swatow to 'Rosamonde Tokio', 3 Apr 1916 (JACAR B03050738800)
sample_original: 潮城由莫擎宇獨立。我軍亦光復汕頭。後莫率大隊來，令我退出鎮守府。
sample_en: Chaozhou city has been declared independent by Mo Qingyu. Our army has also recovered Swatow. Afterwards Mo came at the head of a large force and ordered us out of the garrison headquarters.
why: Short Chinese telegram, decoded character by character with a syllable table; the decipherment is three clean lines with an English translation; one character (翼□) and the last word are garbled, a restored 港 is flagged. Fully readable.

label: No. 1, Vienna, 3 Feb 1720 (R5019 autograph, R5020 copy)
sample_original: ohne einichen geringsten Argwohn mit dem Graf Tarouca von Portugal aus ... die zwischen uns gemachte Tractat geändert würde
sample_en: without any suspicion at all; with Count Tarouca, from Portugal; if the treaty made between us were altered.
why: 26 cipher passages (A-Z) set out in a table (clear lead-in, numbers, key values, reading), each reading a short German phrase, plus a 'What the letter says' summary in English and a separate clear-text transcription; the passages read cleanly (only 446, 638 and a few key slips open) but are fragments in table form, so a reader must stitch them with the clear text. Needs assembling, not more cryptanalysis.
